M1.reason: The side and iso views read as a pistol lying on its side: a long slide, a tall grip slab dropping from its rear half, and a trigger guard loop under the grip (sides.png, below and front-left). The L-shape in the iso and top views is the grip seen against the slide, which matches a pistol on its side. The brief names no other outline. Views are small and low-res, but nothing sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: Measured length is 9.5 against the brief's 10, which is 5% short and inside the 15% band. Width 1.4 and height 8.8 are as the brief implies for a pistol lying on its side.

M3.reason: The parts the brief names are a pistol's slide, barrel, grip and magazine, plus the trigger and guard every Valve gun in lineup.png shows. The slide and muzzle end are in sides.png (right and back). The grip with its magazine slab is in below.png and in-hand.png. The trigger guard is a clear loop in below.png and in-hand.png, and a trigger tab sits inside it. A rear sight block shows in top.png. Nothing named is missing. Front sight and magazine base are not charged.

M4.reason: The brief asks for black and grey polymer and steel. The asset is dark black body with grey upper panels and a grey steel-looking slide top (sides.png, first-person.png). That is the same colour split, with no region the wrong colour.

M5.reason: The brief names no markings, panel lines or wear. Faint slide striations show in first-person.png and nothing added in the views is wrong. Nothing charged.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. In the line-up test the judges picked D (the 9mm submachine gun) as the one not made by Valve in all four orderings, and never the asset (A, B, A, B positions). It passes as one of the game's.

M7.reason: The long axis runs horizontally in the left, right and front views, as a pistol lying on its side on the floor should. The grip falls away from the slide in top.png, so the side it lies on is consistent with the brief. The front is the muzzle end (dark tip in right.png), and the rear block is at the other end.

M8.reason: The triangle count is 216. That is under the 284 limit (twice the median of 142) and under the 291 that Valve's most-used kind spends, so it is within the band. checkErrors is empty. The views show closed solid forms with no open faces where a player can see, and nothing visibly floats.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits in the right hand as the game's pistol does, grip in the palm, muzzle up. In attack.png the weapon stays in the hand across frames 0 to 14 and moves with it, with no point where it parts from the hand. The swing does not carry it out of the picture.
